root_cause.text: Including X86_CR4_FRED in the CR4 pinned bits mask created a boot-time window on APs where FRED MSRs are not yet set up, causing triple faults in SEV-ES/SNP and TDX guests, and the attempted mitigation (temporarily disabling CR4 pinning) introduced an exploitable security vulnerability because an attacker could modify the online bit in writable memory to disable pinning.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and CVE description state that "Commit in Fixes added the FRED CR4 bit to the CR4 pinned bits mask... there's an issue when during boot FRED is initialized: first on the BSP and later on the APs. Thus, there's a window in time when exceptions cannot be handled... triple fault due to FRED MSRs not being set up yet." It further notes that the attempted fix "temporarily disabling CR4 pinning... is a problem in itself because in this case, an attack on the kernel needs to only modify the online bit - a single bit in RW memory - and then disable CR4 pinning and then disable SM*P." The patch removes X86_CR4_FRED from cr4_pinned_mask.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect pinning of the FRED feature by removing it from the CR4 pinned mask.
intent_record.what: Removed X86_CR4_FRED from the cr4_pinned_mask constant definition.
intent_record.how: The set of CR4 bits that are pinned (enforced to remain unchanged after CPU init) no longer includes the FRED bit, allowing it to change or not be restored.
